hypotheses.justification: Connectivity follows from hTau alone. Write R(a,b) = rank(D + a•oneChip u - b•oneChip v). For any natural n, choose A ≥ tau b for 0 ≤ b ≤ n, and L ≤ all those values sufficiently negative that R(L-1,0) = R(L-1,n+1) = -1. Summing hTau.2 over L ≤ a ≤ A and 0 ≤ b ≤ n telescopes to R(A,0) - R(A,n+1) = n+1. Thus R(A,0) ≥ n, using rank_geq_neg_one; the boundary vanishing uses rank_neg_one_of_deg_neg. These lemmas require no connectivity and transfer through rank_toLib. Conversely, a disconnected graph has a nonempty edge-isolated cut S not containing u. Summation over S annihilates every firing vector, hence every principal divisor. Consequently rank(D + A•oneChip u) ≤ max(-1, ∑ x∈S, D x), uniformly in A: removing sufficiently many chips at any vertex of S makes its cut degree negative and therefore unwinnable. This contradicts the arbitrarily large ranks just obtained. The graph is nonempty by its structure, singleton graphs are connected, and coincident marks do not affect this argument. Derive hconn this way, then use the existing proof unchanged.
